questions.question: On what date did President Andrew Jackson sign the act reserving the hot springs in Arkansas?
questions.explanation: Jackson signed the act on April 20, 1832, setting aside the springs and four surrounding sections.

questions.question: How many years older is the 1832 Hot Springs Reservation than Yellowstone National Park?
questions.explanation: NPS calls Hot Springs the oldest national park among current park units, predating Yellowstone by forty years.

questions.question: Which president sent William Dunbar and George Hunter to explore the Ouachita country and its hot springs?
questions.explanation: It was one of only four ventures into the Louisiana Purchase commissioned by Jefferson.

questions.question: What did William Dunbar call the Arkansas hot springs in his August 1804 letter to Thomas Jefferson?
questions.explanation: On Aug. 17, 1804, Dunbar wrote Jefferson about "the boiling springs."

questions.question: How much money did Congress appropriate for the 1804–05 Dunbar–Hunter expedition to the hot springs?
questions.explanation: Congress appropriated $3,000 for the expedition.

questions.question: What injured George Hunter on the 1804 expedition to the Arkansas hot springs?
wrong: A fall into a hot spring
questions.explanation: On Nov. 22, 1804, Hunter's pistol discharged, hurting his thumb and two fingers.

questions.question: From which state did the Belding family come in 1828 to build a small hotel at Hot Springs?
questions.explanation: Ludovicus Belding and his family came from Massachusetts in 1828 and built a small hotel for visitors to the springs.

questions.question: Which Native nation ceded the land around the Arkansas hot springs to the United States in 1818?
questions.explanation: The Quapaw ceded the land on Aug. 24, 1818.

questions.question: During which dates in 1862 was Hot Springs the capital of Arkansas?
questions.explanation: Gov. Henry Rector moved state government to Hot Springs, which was the state capital from May 6 to July 14, 1862.

questions.question: What number New Madrid Certificate was the basis of the Rector family's claim to the Hot Springs land?
questions.explanation: Congress created New Madrid certificates in 1815 for land lost in the 1811-12 quakes; Certificate 467 was sold for $260, then $640, and half of it for $600.
questions.source: Encyclopedia of Arkansas: Rector v. United States

questions.question: In what year was Garland County, Arkansas, created, with Hot Springs as its seat?
questions.explanation: Garland County was created April 5, 1873, from parts of three counties.

questions.question: Novaculite whetstone mining began in the Hot Springs region as early as what year?
questions.explanation: The Arkansas Archeological Survey says whetstone mining has been an Arkansas industry since the early 1800s.

questions.question: Which 1804 expedition sent by Thomas Jefferson visited the Arkansas hot springs?
questions.explanation: NPS: the expedition came in 1804, sent by President Jefferson to explore the southern reaches of the Louisiana Purchase.

questions.question: Before Garland County was created in 1873, Hot Springs' county had its seat at which town near Malvern?
questions.explanation: Garland County was formed in 1873 with Hot Springs as its seat.

questions.question: What was the track gauge of the original Hot Springs Railroad from Malvern?
questions.explanation: The narrow-gauge line was converted to standard gauge in 1889.
questions.source: Encyclopedia of Arkansas: Hot Springs Railroad

questions.question: From which town did Diamond Jo Reynolds's railroad carry visitors to Hot Springs?
questions.explanation: The line cut the 21-mile trip from Malvern from most of a day to about an hour.
questions.source: Encyclopedia of Arkansas: Hot Springs Railroad

questions.question: About how long did it take to convert the Hot Springs Railroad to standard gauge on Oct. 16, 1889?
questions.explanation: The line was converted to standard gauge in about three hours, after several months of preparation.

questions.question: An 1877 Iron Mountain railroad booklet promoted Hot Springs by comparing it to which German spa?
questions.explanation: "The Hot Springs of Arkansas, America's Baden-Baden" was the first booklet advertising the town.
questions.source: NPS: Getting to the American Spa

questions.question: On what date did Congress pass the act establishing the Government Free Bathhouse at Hot Springs?
questions.explanation: The Government free bathhouse for the indigent was established under an act of Congress of December 16, 1878.

questions.question: About how many free baths did the Hot Springs Government Free Bathhouse give in 1919?
questions.explanation: Applicants swore they could not pay; a false oath carried a fine up to $25, up to 30 days in jail, or both.

questions.question: In 1920, what range did single-bath prices at Hot Springs' bathhouses span, before attendant fees?
questions.explanation: Rates were fixed by the Secretary of the Interior; the 1920 scale ran from $0.50 to $0.80 per single bath.

questions.question: How many baths made up a standard prescribed "course" at Hot Springs in 1920?
questions.explanation: A 21-bath course cost $9–$15 in 1920.

questions.question: What was the maximum attendant fee per single bath at Hot Springs in 1920?
questions.explanation: Attendant fees were capped at 20 cents a bath or $4 a course.

questions.question: The Army and Navy Hospital that opened at Hot Springs in 1887 was the nation's first of what kind?
questions.explanation: The Encyclopedia of Arkansas says $100,000 was approved in 1882 and the hospital opened to patients in January 1887, the first such effort in U.S. history.

questions.question: Which religious denomination was organized at a meeting in Hot Springs in April 1914?
questions.explanation: Pentecostal leaders met April 2–12, 1914, to form it.

questions.question: What started Hot Springs' Great Fire of Sept. 5, 1913?
questions.answer: Ironing that set a curtain alight
questions.explanation: Ulma Madlock was ironing at her Church Street home when the iron ignited a curtain.

questions.question: Why were Little Rock's fire hoses useless in Hot Springs' 1913 fire?
questions.answer: They didn't fit Hot Springs hydrants
questions.explanation: Firefighters came by train from Little Rock around 8 p.m., but their hoses did not fit the local hydrants.

questions.question: In which hotel did Hot Springs' deadly Feb. 25, 1905, fire start?
questions.explanation: It began at about 3 a.m.; the cause was never determined, and nearly 400 buildings were destroyed.

questions.question: Roughly how many people were left homeless by Hot Springs' 1913 fire?
questions.explanation: The entry puts the damage at $10 million.

questions.question: Which kind of roof did Hot Springs outlaw after the 1913 fire?
questions.explanation: The town also doubled its fire department.

questions.question: Which fraternal order opened the Pythian Bathhouse and Sanitarium in Hot Springs in 1914?
questions.explanation: It offered half-price baths to Pythian insurance members.
questions.source: NPS: African Americans and the Hot Springs Baths

questions.question: In what year did a great fire sweep up the valley and destroy most of the south and central downtown area of Hot Springs?
questions.explanation: NPS says the great fire of 1878 destroyed most of the south and central downtown area.

questions.question: On what date did the Hot Springs Reservation become Hot Springs National Park?
questions.explanation: NPS: designated the eighteenth national park on March 4, 1921; Congress had established the National Park Service on Aug. 25, 1916.

questions.question: When Hot Springs became a national park in 1921, it was the nation's national park number what?
questions.explanation: It was designated the 18th national park on March 4, 1921.

questions.question: During WWII, Hot Springs' Army-Navy Hospital was the nation's largest center for adults with which disease?
questions.explanation: It was also the Army's leading arthritis center.

questions.question: Which Central Avenue gaming house did Owney Madden eventually come to own a controlling interest in?
questions.explanation: Madden eventually came to own a controlling interest in the Southern Club, a gaming house on Central Avenue.

questions.question: About what share of 1946 primary poll-tax receipts did Judge John Miller throw out in Garland County?
questions.explanation: Receipts came in alphabetical blocks of names that each appeared to be in one person's handwriting.

questions.question: About how many service members did Hot Springs' WWII Army redistribution center process?
questions.explanation: The Army took over most of the hotels in August 1944; the center closed in December 1945.

questions.question: On what date did the second Arlington Hotel burn?
questions.explanation: One fireman died and damage was about $1.6 million.

questions.question: What was Hot Springs' Memorial Field airport first named when dedicated in 1946?
questions.explanation: It was named for Mayor Leo McLaughlin and renamed in May 1947.
questions.source: City of Hot Springs: Airport History

questions.question: In what year did buses replace streetcars in Hot Springs?
questions.explanation: Horsecars had begun in the 1870s; electric cars followed in the 1890s.

questions.question: Which New Deal work program built Lake Catherine State Park near Hot Springs?
questions.explanation: Wikipedia says the park was built in the 1930s by the CCC; three stone-and-wood cabins are on the National Register.

questions.question: What did Judge John Miller call a 'statistical improbability' in ruling on Garland County's 1946 primary poll-tax receipts?
wrong: Receipts lacking the county clerk's seal
questions.explanation: EoA says the receipts were issued in alphabetical order, in blocks of names; the GI ticket then won every seat in Garland County.

questions.question: In what year did passenger rail service to Hot Springs end?
questions.explanation: The entry says the last passenger train to and from Hot Springs, on the Missouri Pacific, ran in 1964.
questions.source: Encyclopedia of Arkansas: Hot Springs Railroad

questions.question: For what price was Hot Springs' Army-Navy Hospital transferred to Arkansas in 1960?
questions.explanation: The grounds were sold to the state for one dollar; the hospital's military era ended April 1, 1960.

questions.question: On what date was Hot Springs' Vapors nightclub bombed?
questions.explanation: Twelve injuries were reported; Gazette reporters photographed the club's slot machines and craps tables.

questions.question: In what year were Hot Springs' bathhouses desegregated?
questions.explanation: School desegregation began in 1956 with a high-school auto-mechanics course.

questions.question: Which group bought Hot Springs' Woodmen of Union Building and ran it as the National Baptist Hotel?
questions.explanation: Wikipedia says the association bought it in 1950; the hotel closed in 1981.

questions.question: According to Wikipedia, in what year did Gov. Winthrop Rockefeller end Hot Springs' casino revival?
questions.explanation: A casino revival during Gov. Orval Faubus's administration (1955-1967) was ended in 1967 by Republican Gov. Winthrop Rockefeller.

questions.question: By 1979, about how many baths a year were given on Hot Springs' Bathhouse Row?
questions.explanation: In 1946 a record 649,270 baths were taken; bathhouse visitation decreased after 1946.

questions.question: On what date did Hot Springs' Majestic Hotel catch fire?
questions.explanation: The Encyclopedia of Arkansas says the downtown landmark caught fire on Feb. 27, 2014.

questions.question: About how much is the Maurice Bathhouse restoration that broke ground in August 2025?
questions.explanation: NPS celebrated the groundbreaking on Aug. 19, 2025; the Maurice is the last Bathhouse Row building to undergo rehabilitation.
questions.source: NPS: Groundbreaking celebrated for Maurice Bathhouse rehabilitation

questions.question: Which national park appeared on the first quarter in the America the Beautiful series, released in 2010?
questions.explanation: The Hot Springs quarter was released April 19, 2010.
questions.source: Encyclopedia of Arkansas: Hot Springs National Park

questions.question: What was the population of the city of Hot Springs in the 2020 census?
questions.explanation: The Encyclopedia of Arkansas lists the city's 2020 Census population as 37,930.

questions.question: Which institute was established in 2009 at the facility that began as Hot Springs' Army and Navy hospital?
questions.explanation: In 1960 the hospital was turned over to the state and became the Hot Springs Rehabilitation Center.
questions.source: UALR Public Radio: EOA Minute, Army-Navy Hospital

questions.question: How many known archeological sites does Hot Springs National Park contain?
questions.explanation: NPS describes a dense, rich archeological record with 92 sites and counting.

questions.question: Whose life-size statue stands in the men's bath hall of the Fordyce Bathhouse?
questions.explanation: The entry describes a life-sized de Soto statue in the men's bath hall; most historians discredit the de Soto legend.

questions.question: In what year did the first Arlington Hotel open in Hot Springs?
questions.explanation: The Arlington's history page says the original hotel opened in 1875 as the state's largest hotel.

questions.question: What was Hot Springs' Majestic Hotel originally called when built in 1882?
questions.explanation: The Avenue Hotel was renamed the Majestic in 1888.
questions.source: Encyclopedia of Arkansas: Central Avenue Historic District

questions.question: What was Hot Springs' Central Avenue originally called before it was named Central Avenue by the late 1870s?
questions.explanation: The street, originally Valley Street, was named Central Avenue by the late 1870s to reflect its status as the commercial center.
questions.source: Encyclopedia of Arkansas: Central Avenue Historic District

questions.question: Which is the oldest surviving bathhouse on Hot Springs' Bathhouse Row?
questions.explanation: EoA calls the Hale, built in 1892-93, the oldest surviving bathhouse; the Buckstaff (1912), Fordyce (1914-15) and Lamar (1923) came later.

questions.question: Which Bathhouse Row bathhouse has offered baths continuously since 1912?
questions.explanation: NPS says the Buckstaff opened on February 1, 1912, and has been in continuous operation since.

questions.question: Which 1904 Hot Springs bathhouse was the first built exclusively for African Americans?
questions.explanation: It stood at 415 Malvern Ave. and burned in the 1913 fire.
questions.source: NPS: African Americans and the Hot Springs Baths

questions.question: What did the Fordyce Bathhouse cost to build in 1914–15, including fixtures?
questions.explanation: The Fordyce was the most elaborate and most expensive of the bathhouses, the cost including fixtures and furniture.

questions.question: Which fountain sits beneath the Fordyce Bathhouse's stained-glass skylight?
questions.explanation: The massive stained-glass skylight is in the men's area, with the DeSoto fountain centered on the floor directly below it.

questions.question: What color are the tile medallions on the Superior Bathhouse facade?
questions.explanation: Concrete on the facade is painted to imitate ornamental tile.

questions.question: What is the name of the Maurice Bathhouse den with an inglenook fireplace?
questions.explanation: The dark-panelled den has an inglenook fireplace with flanking benches and carved mascarons on the ends of the ceiling beams.

questions.question: Which two older bathhouses stood on the site of the 1922 Quapaw Bathhouse?
questions.explanation: The Quapaw was built on the sites of two earlier bathhouses, the Horseshoe and the Magnesia.

questions.question: What color is the brick of the Buckstaff Bathhouse?
questions.explanation: Cream brick with white stucco trim and brass "Buckstaff Baths" letters.

questions.question: What bronze figures guard Bathhouse Row's 1890s main entrance?
questions.explanation: Army engineer Lt. Robert Stevens designed the reservation's entrances, including the historic main entrance.

questions.question: What was the steel observation tower that preceded today's Hot Springs Mountain Tower called?
questions.explanation: The steel Rix Tower, opened in 1906, had an elevator to carry visitors to the top.

questions.question: About how many rooms did Hot Springs' Eastman Hotel have?
questions.explanation: The Baseball Trail calls it 'the elegant, 500-room Eastman Hotel.'
questions.source: Hot Springs Historic Baseball Trail: The Eastman Hotel

questions.question: In what year was the Ohio Club on Hot Springs' Central Avenue founded?
questions.explanation: During Prohibition the Ohio Club officially became the Ohio Cigar Store, a front with a fake wall.

questions.question: In what year was Hot Springs' Southern Club built as a private club?
questions.explanation: Charles Dugan and Dan Stuart built it.

questions.question: Which Bathhouse Row bathhouse has "spring number 46" in a glazed-tile basement room?
questions.explanation: Its basement has a glazed-tile room with an arched ceiling over the natural hot spring; the Hale and Quapaw basements also show springs.

questions.question: In which year was the current (third) Arlington Hotel completed after the 1923 fire?
questions.explanation: Per the Arlington's history page, construction on the third Arlington began Oct. 25, 1923, and the new hotel was completed Nov. 28, 1924.

questions.question: Which bathhouse's 1923 opening completed Hot Springs' Bathhouse Row?
questions.explanation: NPS: the final metamorphosis of Bathhouse Row was completed when the Lamar opened in 1923; it closed in 1985.

questions.question: Why was Hot Springs' Quapaw Bathhouse given its name?
questions.answer: Native artifacts turned up while digging its basement
wrong: A Quapaw chief once owned the site
The 1818 Quapaw treaty was signed there
questions.explanation: The entry says the Quapaw got its name from Indian artifacts found while excavating its basement.

questions.question: What inspired the Maurice Bathhouse's 1931 therapeutic pool?
questions.answer: FDR's treatments at Warm Springs, Ga.
questions.explanation: The entry says the addition was meant to treat various forms of paralysis.

questions.question: In what architectural style was the Hale Bathhouse facade remodeled in 1939–40?
questions.explanation: Thompson, Sanders & Ginocchio's late-1930s remodel changed the facade from neo-Classical revival to Mission Style in 1939-40.

questions.question: What was the Maurice Bathhouse's 1931 therapeutic pool built for?
questions.explanation: The pool was installed in 1931 to treat paralysis; the Maurice was the only bathhouse to employ a registered physical therapist.

questions.question: Which Bathhouse Row bathhouse is crowned by a large tiled dome?
questions.explanation: Its chevron-mosaic dome is topped by a small copper cupola.

questions.question: What was Hot Springs' Quapaw Bathhouse originally going to be named?
questions.explanation: After a tufa cavity turned up during excavation, the owners promoted it as an Indian cave and chose the name Quapaw instead of Platt.

questions.question: Which fish decorates the parapets of Hot Springs' Quapaw Bathhouse?
questions.explanation: Scalloped shells frame the sculpin, originally gold and now white.

questions.question: Which Bathhouse Row bathhouse has twin towers with three-tiered setbacks?
questions.explanation: The 1922 Spanish Colonial Revival design has a vague Art Deco look.

questions.question: In what decade did construction begin on the Grand Promenade behind Bathhouse Row?
questions.explanation: Work began in the 1930s on the promenade behind the bathhouses, which was finally completed in the early 1960s.

questions.question: In what year was the NPS Administration Building on Bathhouse Row built?
questions.explanation: The Spanish Colonial Revival building was designed by NPS architects and still serves as the park's administrative core.

questions.question: After buying the Southern Club building in 1927, what material did William Jacobs use to encase its front, helping hide the gambling?
questions.explanation: Capone reportedly played poker there at an elevated table.

questions.question: Which was the first Bathhouse Row bathhouse to close, in 1962?
questions.explanation: NPS: the Fordyce was the first to close, in 1962, and was later adapted for use as a visitor center and museum.

questions.question: What was built on the site of Hot Springs' demolished Eastman Hotel?
questions.answer: The federal courthouse and post office
questions.explanation: Wikipedia: the Federal Building at 100 Reserve St. was built in 1959-60 on the site of the Eastman Hotel.
questions.source: Wikipedia: Federal Building-U.S. Post Office and Court House (Hot Springs, Arkansas)

questions.question: In what year was the Noble Fountain moved to the Reserve Avenue end of the Grand Promenade?
questions.explanation: The Maurice Spring fountain dates from 1903 and the Administration Building fountain from 1936.

questions.question: When was the jug fountain in front of the NPS Administration Building in Hot Springs installed?
questions.explanation: A new jug fountain on the sidewalk in front of the Administration building was installed in 1966.

questions.question: Which Bathhouse Row building houses Hot Springs National Park's visitor center and museum?
questions.explanation: The Fordyce reopened as the visitor center on May 13, 1989.
questions.source: Encyclopedia of Arkansas: Hot Springs National Park

questions.question: How tall is the Hot Springs Mountain Tower?
questions.explanation: The lattice steel observation tower was officially opened to the public on June 3, 1983.

questions.question: Which gated community near Hot Springs did John A. Cooper Sr. open in 1970?
questions.explanation: It opened June 1, 1970, on about 20,000 acres bought from Dierks Forests.
questions.source: Encyclopedia of Arkansas: Hot Springs Village

questions.question: In what year did the Fordyce Bathhouse reopen as Hot Springs National Park's visitor center?
questions.explanation: The Fordyce closed June 29, 1962, and has served as the park visitor center since 1989.

questions.question: In what month and year did the Lamar Bathhouse stop offering baths?
questions.explanation: The Lamar's baths ended in November 1985, leaving the Buckstaff as the only bathhouse still operating on the Row until the Quapaw reopened in 2008.

questions.question: In what year was Bathhouse Row designated a National Historic Landmark District?
questions.explanation: It was listed on the National Register in 1974 and became an NHL district May 28, 1987.

questions.question: In what month and year did the current Hot Springs Mountain Tower open?
questions.explanation: Construction began in 1982; it opened June 3, 1983.

questions.question: On what date was Hot Springs' Bathhouse Row listed on the National Register of Historic Places?
questions.explanation: NPS: Bathhouse Row and its environs were placed on the National Register of Historic Places on Nov. 13, 1974.

questions.question: Which Bathhouse Row bathhouse is now the nine-suite Hotel Hale?
questions.explanation: NPS says the Hale Bathhouse is now Hotel Hale, with 9 suites whose soaking tubs get hot springs mineral water.

questions.question: Which Bathhouse Row bathhouse now houses a brewery and distillery?
questions.explanation: The Superior Bathhouse Brewery and Distillery has occupied the Superior Bathhouse since 2012.

questions.question: When did Quapaw Baths & Spa open in the restored Quapaw Bathhouse?
questions.explanation: NPS restored the building in 2004.

questions.question: What does the Ozark Bathhouse on Bathhouse Row house today?
questions.explanation: It reopened in 2014 as a cultural center showing artist-in-residence work.

questions.question: Which Bathhouse Row building holds the official park store, the Bathhouse Row Emporium?
questions.explanation: The Lamar also served as interim visitor center while the Fordyce was renovated.

questions.question: What color was the brick of the Majestic Hotel section destroyed by fire in 2014?
questions.explanation: The rest of the condemned hotel was razed in late 2016.

questions.question: What museum now occupies Hot Springs' former Southern Club casino?
questions.explanation: The club stood at 250 Central Avenue.

questions.question: Which 2006 wood-and-glass chapel stands in Garvan Woodland Gardens?
questions.explanation: Designed by architects Maurice Jennings and David McKee of Fayetteville; it officially opened in September 2006.
questions.source: Encyclopedia of Arkansas: Garvan Woodland Gardens

questions.question: How many historic bathhouses stand on Hot Springs' Bathhouse Row?
questions.explanation: Superior, Hale, Maurice, Fordyce, Quapaw, Ozark, Buckstaff and Lamar line Central Avenue.

questions.question: What is the street address of the Buckstaff Bathhouse?
questions.explanation: NPS lists the Buckstaff at 509 Central and the Quapaw at 413 Central.

questions.question: What is the street address of Hot Springs' Arlington Hotel?
questions.explanation: It stands at the "Y" of Central Avenue and Fountain Street.

questions.question: How many successive Arlington Hotel buildings has Hot Springs had?
questions.explanation: They date from 1875, 1892–93 and 1924.

questions.question: How many principal springs did the Dunbar–Hunter expedition count at Hot Springs in 1804?
questions.explanation: They counted four principal springs and two lesser ones.

questions.question: What average water temperature did the Dunbar–Hunter expedition record at the hot springs?
questions.explanation: The explorers measured the water temperature, which averaged between 148 and 150 degrees.

questions.question: What did the Dunbar–Hunter party call the creek, now Gulpha Creek, where it camped in December 1804?
questions.explanation: They camped at the confluence of Calfait Creek (today Gulpha Creek), also called Ellis Landing.

questions.question: In what year was Yale's Bertram Boltwood authorized to study the radioactivity of the Hot Springs waters?
questions.explanation: He concluded the radioactivity came from dissolved radium emanation, a gas, not from radium salts.

questions.question: Which creek flows through a tunnel beneath Hot Springs' Bathhouse Row?
questions.explanation: The government enclosed the creek in an underground arch in 1882-83 for flood and sewerage control.

questions.question: What was the Ouachita National Forest called when it was established in 1907?
questions.explanation: It was renamed on April 29, 1926.

questions.question: In what decade did the government enclose Hot Springs Creek in an underground arch for flood and sewerage control?
questions.explanation: NPS: in 1882-83 the government enclosed Hot Springs creek in an underground arch for flood and sewerage control.

questions.question: In what decade was Hot Springs' Display Spring uncovered so visitors could see thermal water in its natural state?
questions.explanation: It had been covered by a grate for decades.

questions.question: Which dam formed Lake Hamilton, and when was it completed?
questions.explanation: Arkansas Power & Light developed the lake; Carpenter Dam, a concrete gravity dam, was completed in 1931 and the lake was created in 1932.

questions.question: About how many acres is Lake Hamilton?
questions.explanation: Wikipedia gives Lake Hamilton as 7,200 acres; Lake Catherine, the smaller of the two lakes, is about 1,940 acres.

questions.question: Which dam forms Lake Catherine, and when was it built?
questions.explanation: Both Remmel and Carpenter dams were listed on the National Register in 1992.

questions.question: What type of dam is Lake Catherine's Remmel Dam?
questions.explanation: It was built in 1924 by Ford, Bacon & Davis with Ambursen Construction.

questions.question: A 1941 guide called Lake Winona, in the Ouachita National Forest, the principal source of which city's water supply?
questions.explanation: Central Arkansas Water owns Lake Winona, built 1936-38 about 35 miles west of Little Rock.

questions.question: Which dam creates Lake Ouachita near Hot Springs?
questions.explanation: The Army Corps of Engineers built the 231-ft dam from 1948 to 1953.

questions.question: About how many islands does Lake Ouachita have?
questions.explanation: Wikipedia's infobox lists 200 islands for the lake.

questions.question: Which historic healing springs does Lake Ouachita State Park preserve?
questions.explanation: The 360-acre park opened in 1955.

questions.question: In what year did quartz crystal become Arkansas's state mineral?
questions.explanation: EoA says Gov. Winthrop Rockefeller signed Act 128 on Feb. 22, 1967, naming quartz crystal the state mineral.
questions.source: Encyclopedia of Arkansas: Official State Mineral

questions.question: On which river is DeGray Lake, south of Hot Springs?
questions.explanation: The dam is approximately eight miles above the river's confluence with the Ouachita River.

questions.question: According to Wikipedia, DeGray Lake holds the distinction as the first Corps of Engineers impoundment able to do what?
questions.explanation: Wikipedia calls it the first "pump back capable" impoundment in the history of the Corps of Engineers.

questions.question: What is DeGray Lake's maximum depth?
questions.explanation: Its average depth is about 47 ft.

questions.question: What is the largest lake in Hot Springs Village?
questions.explanation: The Hot Springs Village site lists Lake Balboa at 944 acres.
questions.source: Explore the Village (Hot Springs Village): Lakes

questions.question: What is the Arkansas state-record walleye, and where was it caught?
questions.explanation: Al Nelson caught it on March 12, 1982.

questions.question: What is Arkansas's statewide daily limit for black bass?
questions.explanation: The possession limit is triple the daily limit.
questions.source: AGFC: Statewide lengths and daily limits

questions.question: What is Arkansas's statewide daily crappie limit?
questions.explanation: Black and white crappie are combined in the limit; area-specific rules may differ.
questions.source: AGFC: Statewide lengths and daily limits

questions.question: What is the Arkansas state-record striped bass?
questions.explanation: AGFC lists it as caught at Beaver Lake Tailwater on 04/28/2000.

questions.question: Why must Lake Ouachita's striped bass be stocked every year?
questions.explanation: AGFC says striped bass do not reproduce naturally in the wild, apart from one Arkansas River population; Lake Ouachita is one of four lakes it stocks.
questions.source: Arkansas Game & Fish Commission: Striped Bass

questions.question: What tree did AGFC and the Corps mostly use for new Lake Ouachita fish brush piles?
questions.explanation: AGFC said the brush piles would sit in the 20- to 25-foot range most of the year, on points near the mid-lake islands.
questions.source: AGFC: Improving angling odds at Lake Ouachita

questions.question: What lure caught the 11-lb Lake Hamilton largemouth at a May 2024 club tournament?
questions.explanation: The color was Green Pumpkin Magic.
questions.source: AGFC: Tourney anglers catch a couple of whopper bass in Lake Hamilton

questions.question: How many acres is Garvan Woodland Gardens on Lake Hamilton?
questions.explanation: The University of Arkansas owns the garden.

questions.question: How many miles of trail make up Phase One of Hot Springs' Northwoods trail system, which began opening in 2018?
questions.explanation: Seven of Phase I's 14 miles opened Nov. 17, 2018; the finished system is described as about 44 miles.

questions.question: What does the name of novaculite, the Ouachita whetstone rock, mean in Latin?
questions.explanation: Novaculite takes its name from the Latin for "razor stone."

questions.question: What two industry grades are Garland County novaculite whetstones sold as?
questions.explanation: "Washita" is duller and porous; "Arkansas" is finer-grained, waxy and denser.

questions.question: About how old is most Hot Springs thermal water, per USGS tritium and carbon-14 dating?
questions.explanation: USGS found the water is a mix: a very small amount under 20 years old and a preponderance about 4,400 years old.

questions.question: Per the National Park Service, about how much water do the Hot Springs thermal springs produce per day?
questions.explanation: NPS says the springs produce over 700,000 gallons of water a day.

questions.question: What is the average temperature of Hot Springs' thermal spring water?
questions.explanation: NPS calls them the hottest springs east of the Rocky Mountains.

questions.question: According to the USGS, how many hot springs emerge from Hot Springs Mountain in Hot Springs National Park?
questions.explanation: USGS says the park is best known for its 47 hot springs, which emerge from Hot Springs Mountain at an average temperature of 143 degrees Fahrenheit.

questions.question: Which two dating methods showed most Hot Springs thermal water is about 4,400 years old?
questions.explanation: USGS Professional Paper 1044-C found a small share of water under 20 years old.

questions.question: Outcrops of which two rock formations recharge the Hot Springs thermal springs?
questions.explanation: USGS: rainfall infiltrates the outcrops, and the water moves slowly to depth where rocks heat it.

questions.question: What are the names of the two faults the National Park Service says help carry Hot Springs' heated water back to the surface?
questions.explanation: NPS says fault lines help direct the heated water back to the surface.

questions.question: Which downtown Hot Springs streets does the "alpha" fault roughly follow?
questions.explanation: The beta fault follows the top edge of Hot Springs Mountain.

questions.question: About how hot does Hot Springs' rainwater get deep underground before it rises?
questions.explanation: It heats through the geothermal gradient roughly a mile down.

questions.explanation: KKYR says at least three scenes were shot in Arkansas, including at the Arlington Resort Hotel and the Fordyce Bath House; most scenes were filmed in Alabama.

questions.question: Which Hot Springs racetrack's winter-spring meet is sometimes called the "Fifth Season"?

questions.question: What do historians conclude about the legend that Hernando de Soto bathed at Hot Springs in 1541?
questions.answer: There is no firm evidence he visited
wrong: Spanish coins found there prove it

questions.question: Which stone did Native peoples quarry in the hills around Hot Springs for thousands of years?
questions.explanation: Indians quarried novaculite from bedrock deposits in the hills around Hot Springs for many thousands of years.

questions.question: Hot Springs National Park began in 1832 as what kind of protected land?
questions.explanation: EOA calls it the nation's first federal reservation.

questions.question: How did railroad builder Joseph "Diamond Jo" Reynolds get his nickname?
questions.answer: He marked shipments "Jo" inside a diamond
wrong: He wore a huge diamond ring
He won a diamond mine at cards
His first boat was the Diamond
questions.explanation: He created the trademark after another J. Reynolds caused confusion among customers.
questions.source: Encyclopedia of Arkansas: Hot Springs Railroad

questions.question: What was "Ral City" in 19th-century Hot Springs?
questions.answer: A camp of poor health seekers at Ral Spring
questions.explanation: Because Ral Spring was free, it drew hundreds of health seekers who could not afford bathhouse fees; the encampment around the spring became known as Ral City.

questions.question: The name of Hot Springs' Ral Spring was likely short for what word?
questions.explanation: NPS says "neuralgia" was also another term for symptoms of syphilis, a venereal disease.

questions.explanation: Wikipedia says the wireless telegraph tower from the 1904 Louisiana Purchase Exposition was moved to the mountain in 1906.

questions.question: What title does Hot Springs promote itself with in baseball history?
wrong: Home of the first night game

questions.question: Where did Babe Ruth's first home run of March 17, 1918, in Hot Springs land?

questions.question: What did Hot Springs' Government Free Bathhouse provide?
questions.answer: Free baths for those who couldn't pay

questions.question: From where did H. L. Campbell bring the first alligators for Hot Springs' alligator farm?

questions.question: What did Tiny Town creator Frank Moshinskie make out of cat-food cans?

questions.explanation: It is also an Oscar qualifier.

questions.question: Which Arlington Hotel floor is the "woman in a white gown" said to haunt?
